title: KScript standard (kscript-standard.json)
description: A shareable set of lint rules and format settings. A project uses it with "standard" in kscript.json, and another standard can build on it with "extends". Later layers win: the standards it extends, then this one, then the project's kscript.json.

standardReference.description: kscript:recommended, kscript:strict, or a path (relative to this file) to a standard file or a folder holding kscript-standard.json.

name.description: The standard's name, shown by kscript check --print-config.

extends.description: Standards this one builds on. They are applied first, so this one's settings win. Without extends, a standard starts from the built-in defaults, where style rules (KS6xxx) are off: extend kscript:recommended to keep them.

lint.description: Lint rules this standard sets. Which files are checked (include, exclude) belongs in each project's kscript.json.

rules.description: Severity per diagnostic code (KS3003) or code prefix (KS3*). The longest match wins.

warnings_as_errors.description: Make kscript check fail on warnings too (same as --warnings-as-errors).

format.description: Format settings this standard sets. Which files are formatted (include, exclude) belongs in each project's kscript.json.

enabled.description: false turns formatting off for the project: kscript fmt skips its files and Format Document makes no changes.

rules.description: Turn individual formatting rules off, e.g. { "statement_per_line": false }. Every rule is on unless listed. To leave part of a file alone, use <!-- kscript-fmt: off --> ... <!-- kscript-fmt: on --> or <!-- kscript-fmt-ignore --> before an element.

indent.description: Re-indent elements by how deeply they are nested. Off: lines keep their indentation.

statement_per_line.description: Put each statement and block-level element on its own line. Off: line breaks only change where there was already whitespace.

tidy_tags.description: One space between attributes, and <x /> for self-closing tags. Off: start tags are kept exactly as written.

wrap_attributes.description: One attribute per line for long start tags and tags already written that way. Off: tags are never wrapped or joined.

trim_trailing_whitespace.description: Remove spaces at the ends of lines of text.

collapse_blank_lines.description: Shrink runs of blank lines to max_blank_lines.

final_newline.description: End the file with exactly one newline. Off: the file ends as it did.

spacing.description: .kscript files: one space after commas and colons, around assignments and =>, and before a block's '{'. Off: spacing inside lines is kept.

brace_style.description: .kscript files: put else, elif, catch and finally on the line of the closing '}'. Off: they stay where they are.

wrap_strings.description: .kscript files: break a string that runs past print_width at a space, with a \ at the end of the line (the break isn't part of the string). Off: long strings stay on one line.

wrap_chains.description: .kscript files: a -> chain or |> pipe that runs past print_width puts each call on its own line, indented under where the chain starts. Off: chains stay on one line.

wrap_bodies.description: .kscript files: a one-line function (fn name() => body) that runs past print_width moves its body to the next line. Off: it stays on one line.

wrap_comments.description: .kscript files: a // or /// comment line that runs past print_width is broken between words onto a new comment line. Off: comments stay as written.

indent.description: Spaces per indent level, or "tab" to indent with tabs.

tab_width.description: With "indent": "tab", how many columns a tab counts as when lining up existing text.

print_width.description: The longest a line should be (80 by default). Longer lines are wrapped: a start tag gets one attribute per line, and in .kscript files a long call, chain, one-line function, string or comment is broken onto more lines.

max_blank_lines.description: Blank lines kept in a row; extra ones are removed.

end_of_line.description: Line endings to write. auto keeps the ones each file already uses.

preserve.description: Elements whose content is kept exactly as written, on top of <pre>, <textarea>, <script>, <style> and CDATA sections.
